coverage_gaps: Need Layer 1B evidence on company-level revenue exposure before creating any public-market candidate list.
Need current market-pricing checks: valuation multiples, short interest, earnings revisions, ETF flows, and consensus growth expectations by consumer sub-industry.
Need segmentation by income cohort because high-income discretionary, middle-income value seeking, and lower-income credit stress can produce opposite signals.
Need geographic split: U.S.-only versus global consumer exposure, China exposure, Europe travel, and emerging-market staples demand.
Need policy/tariff verification for 2026 because import costs can materially alter apparel, electronics, home goods, ecommerce sellers, and discount retail margins.
Need brand-level channel mix: wholesale, DTC, marketplace, retail media spend, owned stores, international franchise, and subscription/loyalty dependence.

evidence.claim: U.S. Census reported Q1 2026 adjusted retail ecommerce sales of $326.7 billion, up 2.7% from Q4 2025 and up 9.8% year over year, while total retail sales grew 3.9% year over year.

evidence.claim: The National Retail Federation forecast 2026 retail sales growth of 4.4% over 2025 to $5.6 trillion, citing continued consumer resilience.

evidence.claim: U.S. Travel Association forecast total U.S. travel spending of $1.37 trillion in 2026 and $1.42 trillion in 2027 in inflation-adjusted terms.
IATA reported January 2026 global passenger demand growth of 3.8%, with North America showing much lower growth than several international regions.
evidence.source_title: 2026 Begins with 3.8% Air Passenger Demand Growth

evidence.claim: Skai and Stratably's 2026 State of Retail Media Report said seven in ten surveyed advertisers now meet or exceed retail media performance goals, indicating retail media has become a material channel for consumer brands.
evidence.source_title: Retail Media Reaches Inflection Point as GenAI and Omnichannel Strategies Reshape Advertising Spend

evidence.claim: Deloitte's 2026 retail outlook survey reported that a large majority of retail executives expect trade spend to be diverted to retail media networks, supporting the hypothesis that retailer-owned media can shift profit pools.

The April 2026 BLS CPI release provides category-level inflation data for shelter, food, food away from home, and travel-related items, which should be used in later layers to separate nominal growth from real volume growth.

memory_update.text: Consumer theme should be researched as a set of spending reallocations: essentials/value, ecommerce data monetization, travel experiences, housing repair substitution, staples inputs, and consumer credit/data rails.
Retail media and first-party shopper data are likely a higher-quality chokepoint than generic ecommerce volume because retailers can monetize search, ads, attribution, and seller access.

Housing-linked consumer spend should split transaction-dependent categories from repair/maintenance categories because low existing-home sales can hurt furniture and appliances while supporting necessary repair.
Travel should be decomposed by capacity and packaging: cruises, hotels, OTAs, airlines, events, and inbound travel have different bottlenecks and margin drivers.
Need Layer 1B searches for tariffs/import exposure, consumer credit stress, and income-cohort spending to avoid overgeneralizing consumer resilience.

layer1a.summary: Consumer is too broad to research ticker-first. Layer 1A decomposes it into six investable chokepoint lanes: value-seeking retail and staples, ecommerce plus retail media, travel experiences, housing-linked demand, food and consumables input chains, and consumer credit/data rails. The strongest first-pass Serenity angles are not generic discretionary exposure but nodes where demand remains resilient while control points are scarce: first-party shopper data, retail media monetization, fulfillment/returns economics, affordable travel packaging, housing repair/remodel substitution for low home turnover, and private-label/value supply chains.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: The chokepoint may be purchasing scale plus private-label sourcing capability. Retailers with dense stores, membership ecosystems, vendor leverage, and efficient inventory turns can convert weak discretionary demand into share gains and advertising/data monetization.
supply_chain_nodes.node: Value retail, clubs, off-price, dollar/value channels, and private-label staples
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Map large-format value retailers, warehouse clubs, off-price apparel/home retailers, grocery chains, dollar stores, private-label manufacturers, and CPG companies with defensible value brands. Check same-store sales, traffic versus ticket, gross margin, private-label penetration, shrink, inventory turns, and membership renewal rates.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: The scarce layer is not generic online selling; it is scaled first-party transaction data plus ad inventory plus attribution. Platforms that own demand discovery and checkout can tax brands through retail media, marketplace fees, and fulfillment services.

Verify disclosed ad revenue, take rate, seller services, ad load, conversion ROI, and whether retail media shifts dollars from trade spend or incremental marketing budgets.

supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: As ecommerce share rises, consumer brands increasingly pay for visibility at the point of purchase. Retailers with closed-loop purchase data can monetize traffic through high-margin advertising while brands face rising dependence on sponsored placement.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: The chokepoint is unit economics at order level: inventory placement, automation, package density, returns disposition, and carrier negotiation. Companies that lower delivery and return cost per order can compound share even if category growth is modest.
supply_chain_nodes.node: Fulfillment density, last-mile delivery, reverse logistics, and returns processing
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Map parcel carriers, 3PLs, warehouse automation, returns platforms, omnichannel retailers with store-as-fulfillment capability, packaging suppliers, and software vendors for inventory orchestration. Track fulfillment cost as percentage of sales, return rates by category, delivery speed promises, and capex intensity.

supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: Ecommerce growth does not automatically create profit. Low-margin categories can be destroyed by shipping, labor, split shipments, return rates, and inventory misplacement. The node separates profitable omnichannel operators from volume-only ecommerce exposure.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: The attractive chokepoints may be packaged value travel, cruise capacity, loyalty distribution, hotel supply in constrained event markets, and online platforms with demand aggregation. The weaker lane may be undifferentiated air capacity if costs absorb demand growth.

supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: Travel is a large consumer discretionary category with different economics from goods. Demand can remain resilient when consumers prioritize experiences, but pricing power depends on capacity, labor, aircraft supply, lodging supply, and destination/event calendars.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: The chokepoint is the installed base of aging homes plus service capacity rather than new-home transaction volume. Winners may be retailers and suppliers exposed to necessary repair, pro-contractor demand, HVAC/plumbing/electrical replacement, and small-ticket projects; discretionary furnishings may lag.

supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Map home-improvement retailers, building-products suppliers, HVAC/plumbing distributors, appliance makers, furniture retailers, home-services platforms, paint/flooring companies, storage/moving, and single-family rental operators. Track existing-home sales, mortgage rates, pro versus DIY mix, average ticket, inventory, and project backlog.

supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: Housing turnover normally drives big-ticket consumer categories such as furniture, appliances, flooring, paint, moving, and renovation. When affordability and mortgage lock-in suppress transactions, demand may rotate toward repair, maintenance, smaller projects, rental upgrades, and professional services.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: The chokepoint may be categories where supply is hard to flex quickly, such as protein processing, specialty ingredients, cold-chain capacity, aluminum/glass/paper packaging, and refrigerated distribution. Consumer brands without pricing power may be squeezed between retailers and input suppliers.
supply_chain_nodes.node: Staples input chains: food ingredients, protein, beverages, packaging, cold chain, and wholesale distribution
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Map CPG staples, grocery retailers, protein processors, beverage companies, packaging suppliers, cold-storage REITs/operators, foodservice distributors, and ingredient companies. Check volume versus price mix, gross margin bridge, commodity hedges, promotional spend, retailer concentration, and private-label share loss.

demand_drivers: Household budget bifurcation: essentials and value channels gain share when consumers trade down, while premium discretionary becomes more dependent on high-income resilience.
Ecommerce continues taking share from total retail, increasing the importance of fulfillment density, returns processing, marketplace ranking, and retail media monetization.
Travel remains a large experience-spending pool, but growth appears uneven across domestic leisure, international inbound, business travel, cruises, hotels, and air capacity.
Housing affordability and low existing-home turnover shift consumer spend from transaction-linked categories toward repair, maintenance, rentership, small-ticket renovation, and home services.
Staples and food demand is defensive, but margin capture depends on commodity inputs, private label, packaging, cold chain, distribution efficiency, and pricing power.
Consumer brands increasingly compete through data-driven distribution: retail media, loyalty programs, BNPL/payment rails, subscriptions, and marketplace algorithms.
theme_map.public_market_search_strategy: Start broad by node, not ticker. For each node, screen public companies and ETFs by revenue exposure, margin sensitivity, pricing power, data ownership, and bottleneck control. Search first for primary/official data: Census retail/ecommerce, BLS CPI categories, NAR housing, TSA/IATA/U.S. Travel, company 10-K/10-Q filings, earnings-call transcripts, investor days, and retail media segment disclosures. Then map public assets across retailers, marketplaces, payment networks, logistics providers, travel platforms, hotels/cruises/airlines, home-improvement retailers, food producers, packaging/cold-chain suppliers, and consumer-finance platforms. Avoid ranking securities until Layer 1B/2 verifies revenue exposure, current valuation expectations, and falsification metrics.
supply_side_constraints: High customer-acquisition costs and privacy limits make profitable direct-to-consumer growth harder without first-party data or marketplace scale.
Retail media inventory, closed-loop measurement, and retailer first-party data are controlled by a limited set of large retailers and marketplaces.
Last-mile delivery, reverse logistics, and inventory positioning remain structurally expensive for low-margin ecommerce categories.
Housing affordability, mortgage lock-in, and low inventory constrain big-ticket home-related discretionary demand even when household formation continues.
Food, beverage, and household staples face input-cost volatility, labor costs, packaging costs, and promotional intensity.
Travel capacity can be constrained by aircraft availability, labor, hotel supply in event markets, visa/entry processing, and destination-specific infrastructure.
